title: 10/10 things quietly wrecking your mornings
why: Real tips earn the one confession slide where the app appears, exactly like ReadUp on slide 4.
caption: number 3 is the one nobody wants to hear. which number got you? #morningroutine #screentimehacks #phoneaddiction #sleep
sound: something moody at low volume (the original used deftones)
check: slide 4: 'lasted 2 nights' in the kitchen. Only keep it if it's true for you

slides.heading: checking your phone _before your feet touch the floor_
slides.top: the first thing your brain gets every day is _other people's lives_, your inbox, and a pile of notifications
slides.text:
you haven't decided anything yet and you're already _reacting_

then you wonder why the day feels like it's _running you_
slides.bottom: the first ten minutes set the mood for the next ten hours

slides.heading: the _9 more minutes_ lie
slides.top: snooze, doze, snooze, doze, and you get up _groggier_ than if you'd just got up the first time
slides.text:
the alarm isn't the problem

_staying horizontal_ is, because lying down with your phone in reach is how 9 minutes turns into 40

slides.heading: your phone _sleeps next to you_
slides.top: it's the last thing you see at night and the first thing you grab in the morning
slides.text:
i tried leaving it in the kitchen. _lasted 2 nights_

what actually worked: my apps _go to sleep at 11_ and don't wake up until i've _walked 500 steps_ in the morning

slides.heading: _no daylight_ for the first hour
slides.top: blinds shut, screen brightness up, and your body still thinks it's _the middle of the night_
slides.text:
you feel half awake until lunch and blame your sleep

open the curtains _before_ you open instagram

slides.heading: a _different bedtime_ every night
slides.top: 11pm on monday, 2am on friday, 12:30 on sunday "to reset"
slides.text:
your body never knows when morning is supposed to start

a _boring, same every night_ bedtime does more than any supplement
